codeReview.summary: The feature commit only added test coverage. It does not implement the public booking lifecycle UI/route changes described in the feature contract, and one of the added assertions codifies the wrong shared-detail behavior for the public route.

issues.description: The new 'passes the same shared detail model to the guest booking detail route' test never exercises the public `/bookings/[bookingId]` route and only asserts that the guest route returns a truthy page. That misses the contract that public and guest booking detail must share one model while preserving route-appropriate behavior on the public route, so the feature's core reuse requirement remains unverified. The later fix feature `fix-public-booking-detail-return-intent` exists because this gap shipped.

The unauthenticated public detail assertion expects a direct sign-in redirect from `/bookings/[bookingId]`. The implemented product behavior routes public detail through `/bookings/recover?next=...` before sign-in so recovery continuity and token stripping can work. This test encoded the wrong contract for the public route, which scrutiny later had to correct with follow-up fixes.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The `guest-ui-worker` skill says to write a targeted RED test proving the intended behavior before implementation. The worker added only tests, but those tests did not exercise the public shared-detail reuse path and one asserted the wrong redirect contract, so the procedure as applied did not protect the feature's main requirement.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Skill file `.factory/skills/guest-ui-worker/SKILL.md` step 4 requires RED coverage proving intended guest behavior; transcript/handoff for session `b196dee9-8565-422e-bd28-ef8d7db710a0` shows only `tests/guest/public-booking-pages.test.tsx` was added in commit `aedf616e`, and that file's lines 148-152 and 168-199 miss/misstate the public-route contract.

summary: Fail: commit `aedf616e` adds tests only, and the new coverage does not actually verify the public shared-detail behavior while also baking in an incorrect public redirect expectation. The feature contract was therefore not fully covered by this implementation.
